purpose: Closest-prior screening for compressed directory-constrained single-vector top-k; not new performance experiments or a claim of complete novelty screening

records.title: iFVS: Towards Instance-Optimized Filtered Vector Search
records.formal_venue: 未核实；HTML workshop template is incomplete
read_evidence: section 2: fixed PQ codes/base codebook, query+predicate-dependent codebook perturbation and dimension weights
section 3: FAISS baselines use one CPU thread; iFVS training and inference use NVIDIA A30
section 3.3.1 and Table 2: aggregate figure recall includes training and test; table separates them
section 4: author future work includes unseen-query generalization and workload-shift self-adjustment
records.implication: Filter-conditioned quantized scoring is direct prior art; directory-conditioned codebooks alone are not established novelty
open_items: whether a directory-topology MOVE/MERGE protocol exists in later versions

records.title: Locally Optimized Product Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
read_evidence: section 4.1: per-cell residual rotation/product quantizer and per-cell query lookup
section 6: discussion of mixture fitting and set-compression trees
records.implication: Local residual/PQ optimization and per-partition quantizers are existing techniques, not new merely because a partition is named Node

records.title: SymphonyQG: Towards Symphonious Integration of Quantization and Graph for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
read_evidence: sections 3.1-3.2: graph/quantization co-design, implicit refinement, accelerated graph construction
introduction: compact adjacency/code layout also retains raw vectors
records.implication: Quantized graph search, batched scoring and implicit exact refinement are not novel combinations by themselves
open_items: complete filter-aware applicability and raw-memory accounting

records.title: When Does Low-Bit Quantization Preserve the Decisions of Vector Search?
read_evidence: abstract only: decision flips, exact-margin mass, residual tails and frozen graph-pruning replay
records.implication: MSE reduction alone is not adequate evidence of ranking or graph-pruning preservation
open_items: relevance to filtered margins and directory scopes

researcher_hypothesis_not_author_claim: Frozen global codes with mergeable low-rank quantization-error summaries for laminar scope calibration and MOVE-stable encoding state; novelty and ranking benefit unverified

retracted_hypotheses.hypothesis: Per-scope mean/低秩均值校准 of reconstructed vectors improves DSQ top-k
retracted_hypotheses.reason: Within-scope ranking compares d_hat(q,y)-d_hat(q,x); any additive scope bias cancels and positive scale preserves order, so a mean correction is a ranking no-op. Independently consistent with arXiv:2609.09854 section 3.3, where the affine intercept survives only in alpha!=1 pruning as (1-alpha)b.

usable_results: flip probability bounded by boundary mass plus residual tail
ranking difference-residual scale nu^2 = K_xx + K_yy - 2K_xy
